# Finance and Accounting Stage Contracts

One entry per desk in the Finance Accounting Command Desk suite. Use these when running the suite as a continuous cycle, so a desk can carry the work into the next stage instead of telling the user to invoke another skill.

## Stage order

```text
accounting-policy-coa-desk
  -> revenue-recognition-desk
  -> billing-order-to-cash-desk
  -> accounts-receivable-collections-desk
  -> spend-approval-authority-desk
  -> accounts-payable-desk
  -> expense-management-desk
  -> equity-cap-table-desk
  -> month-end-close-desk
  -> account-reconciliation-desk
  -> tax-coordination-desk
  -> financial-reporting-desk
  -> cash-flow-treasury-desk
  -> saas-metrics-reporting-desk
  -> budget-planning-desk
  -> forecast-scenario-desk
  -> variance-analysis-desk
  -> internal-controls-desk
  -> audit-support-desk
```

The order is a dependency chain, not a mandatory itinerary. Most requests run a subsequence and enter partway: a non-standard order form enters at `revenue-recognition-desk`, a customer who stopped paying enters at `accounts-receivable-collections-desk`, a payment that has to go out today enters at `accounts-payable-desk`, a board deadline enters at `financial-reporting-desk` and pushes backward into close, and an auditor request enters at `audit-support-desk` and pushes backward into whichever account it touches. Never run a stage ahead of the packet state it consumes, and never skip a stage the ledger shows is load bearing for the requested outcome. Record every skip with its reason.

The transaction cycle desks between `revenue-recognition-desk` and `expense-management-desk` operate on separate populations and separate subledgers, so they fan out and converge at `month-end-close-desk`. `account-reconciliation-desk` sits after close because a reconciliation against a moving trial balance is redone the moment the next entry posts. `financial-reporting-desk` sits after `tax-coordination-desk` because the provision lands in the statements, and after reconciliation because a statement produced from an unreconciled ledger is a draft regardless of how finished it looks.

Each entry states the hard halt specific to that stage. The default posture everywhere else is to proceed with the assumption labeled inline against the account, contract, entity, or line item it affects, per `references/halt-taxonomy.md`.

## Contracts

### accounting-policy-coa-desk
Requires: the reporting framework and any statutory or local requirements in force, existing accounting policy memos and the elections already taken, the current chart of accounts with its natural account, department, entity, and any other segments, the materiality policy and its benchmark, the transaction types the business actually generates, prior auditor comments on policy or presentation, planned changes to the business model that the current policy does not contemplate.
Owns: the chart of accounts structure with the rule that decides which account a transaction hits, the segment design covering entity, department, and any product or project dimension, the accounting policy set covering revenue, capitalization, prepaid and accrual thresholds, fixed asset lives, allowance methodology, and lease treatment, technical accounting memos that state the facts, the standard, the analysis, and the conclusion separately, the materiality thresholds with the benchmark and who set them, mapping tables between the operational systems and the ledger, the policy conflicts where written policy and actual practice diverge, and the account additions or retirements proposed with their impact on comparatives.
Hands to: `revenue-recognition-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A chart of accounts change or a policy election changes how every future transaction is classified and breaks the comparability of the periods on either side of it. The controller owns the ledger structure, and a policy election that affects reported results is a decision with the auditor in the room. Prepare the memo and the mapping; the change is applied by the person who owns the consequence.

### revenue-recognition-desk
Requires: the executed contracts including order forms, amendments, side letters, and acceptance provisions, the revenue policy and the elections it takes, standalone selling price evidence, delivery and usage records establishing when control transferred, the billing schedule for each contract, prior period treatment for comparable contracts, sales compensation arrangements where they affect the transaction price, the period status.
Owns: the five step analysis per contract in writing, performance obligations identified with why each is distinct, transaction price including variable consideration with the constraint applied and the evidence for it, allocation across obligations with the standalone selling price basis, the recognition pattern with its measure of progress, the revenue schedule per contract and the deferred revenue waterfall that ties to the balance sheet, contract asset and liability positions, modification accounting for change orders with the rule that decides prospective against cumulative catch-up treatment, the non-standard terms register covering acceptance clauses, service credits, termination for convenience, and side letters, and the contracts whose treatment the available evidence cannot settle, named rather than defaulted to the pattern the last one used.
Hands to: `billing-order-to-cash-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. The contract, the order form, the billing system, and the sales record disagree on term, price, scope, or delivery date. Revenue is the account external readers care most about and the one with the highest restatement rate, and a side letter that nobody routed to finance changes the accounting for a contract that already looked settled. Record every reading with its document, and route the conflict rather than adopting whichever version the system happens to hold.

### billing-order-to-cash-desk
Requires: the revenue schedules and contract terms from the prior stage, the billing system configuration including plans, proration, and tax handling, the invoice run for the period, order form to invoice mapping, usage records where billing is consumption based, credit memo and refund history with the approvals behind them, the customer master and its billing contacts, the cutoff date.
Owns: the billing run reviewed against contract terms rather than against last month's invoice, the exception list covering contracts billed at the wrong amount, on the wrong schedule, or not at all, unbilled revenue where performance precedes the right to invoice, over-billing where cash was collected ahead of performance, the invoice to revenue tie showing where billed and recognized amounts legitimately differ and where they differ because something is wrong, proration and mid-term change handling, credit memo proposals with the reason and the approval each requires, tax and jurisdiction treatment applied on the invoice, and the billing configuration defects that will keep producing the same exception until they are fixed.
Hands to: `accounts-receivable-collections-desk`.
Hard halt: production or destructive. Issuing an invoice, a credit memo, or a refund is an act against a customer that changes the receivable, the revenue, and frequently the relationship. A credit memo in particular is the mechanism by which revenue is quietly reversed, which is exactly why its approval sits above the person who raised the invoice. Prepare the document with its contract basis; a named approver releases it.

### accounts-receivable-collections-desk
Requires: the receivable subledger with invoice level detail and payment application, the aging as of the reporting date, customer payment terms from the contracts rather than from the invoice template, cash application records, dispute and support ticket history, the credit policy and any credit limits in force, the allowance methodology, prior write-offs and recoveries, the collections owner per account.
Owns: the aging with its buckets tied to the general ledger control account, days sales outstanding with the formula stated because the two common formulas give different answers, the exposure ranking by balance and by days past due, dispute analysis separating a delivery problem from a billing error from a customer who is simply not paying, the collections plan with the action, the owner, and the date per account, escalation steps tied to the contract's remedies rather than to a generic dunning ladder, the expected credit loss calculation with its methodology and its roll-forward, write-off candidates with the evidence of uncollectibility and the approval each requires, cash application exceptions including unapplied receipts and short payments, and the concentration risk where a small number of customers carry most of the balance.
Hands to: `spend-approval-authority-desk`, and into `cash-flow-treasury-desk` for the collection timing the forecast depends on.
Hard halt: approval. Writing off a receivable, granting an extended payment plan, releasing a credit hold, or changing a customer's terms each gives away money or risk. The write-off is the one that matters most, because it removes an asset and closes the file, and the fastest way to make an aging look healthy is to write off what is old rather than collect it.

### spend-approval-authority-desk
Requires: the delegation of authority matrix and the board resolutions behind it, the approved budget and the specific line a request would consume, the purchase request or commitment with its amount, term, and total contract value rather than only its first invoice, the vendor and any existing agreement with them, the requester and their approval chain, prior exceptions granted, the procurement process where one exists.
Owns: the authority determination naming the approver the policy requires and the provision that sets the level, the total commitment view including renewal terms and auto-renewal exposure so a monthly figure is not approved as though it were the whole obligation, the budget check identifying the line the spend consumes and the headroom remaining on it, the split-purchase test where a commitment appears sized to sit under an approval threshold, the accounting treatment the commitment will require once it lands, the exception record with who authorized it and why, and the commitments that entered without approval, reported as unapproved rather than backfilled with an approver who would probably have said yes.
Hands to: `accounts-payable-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. This desk exists to enforce an approval gate, so it never grants one. Determining that a commitment needs a named authority and then proceeding without it defeats the only control in the sequence. Where spend has already been committed without approval, that is a control finding routed to `internal-controls-desk`, not a paperwork problem to be tidied.

### accounts-payable-desk
Requires: the payable subledger, vendor invoices for the period, purchase orders and receiving records where the process uses them, the approved vendor master with bank details, contracts and statements of work behind recurring charges, payment terms and any early payment discounts, the payment calendar and available cash, prior duplicate and fraud incidents, tax reporting requirements for vendor payments.
Owns: the three way match with exceptions classified by cause covering price, quantity, and missing receipt, the accrual for goods and services received and not invoiced with how completeness was established rather than assumed, the payment proposal with its date, its total, and the discounts captured or forgone, duplicate detection across vendor, amount, and reference including near matches that the exact match misses, vendor master change review with bank detail changes confirmed through a channel other than the one that requested them, coding review so an invoice hits the account and the period the policy requires, the aging of payables with any invoices held past terms and why, vendor tax reporting classifications, and the recurring charges with no contract behind them, named rather than paid because they were paid last month.
Hands to: `expense-management-desk`.
Hard halt: production or destructive. Releasing a payment run moves money out of the company and is not reversible by editing anything. Payment fraud enters through exactly this stage, and the pattern is consistent: a bank detail change, an urgent request, and an approval chain short-circuited by the deadline. Prepare the run with its evidence; a named approver with payment authority releases it, and a bank detail change is verified out of band before it is used.

### expense-management-desk
Requires: the travel and expense policy in force, submitted expense reports with their receipts and approvals, corporate card statements and transaction feeds, unsubmitted card spend, the employee and cost center mapping, per diem and mileage rates where the policy uses them, prior policy exceptions and how they were handled, tax treatment for benefits and non-deductible categories.
Owns: policy compliance review naming the specific provision breached rather than a general judgment, the out of policy register with the amount, the employee, the approver who let it through, and the disposition, the corporate card reconciliation covering spend without a submitted report and the accrual it drives, the coding review that puts entertainment, benefits, and non-deductible items where tax treatment requires, personal expense identification with the recovery mechanism, the manager approval pattern where one approver clears everything without exception, the accrual for the period covering incurred and unsubmitted spend, and the policy gaps where the spend is legitimate and the policy simply does not address it.
Hands to: `equity-cap-table-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. Expense detail exposes individual travel, health, and personal circumstances, and card data is payment data. An artifact that names employees alongside their spending detail leaves the finance function and becomes an HR matter. Aggregate by cost center and policy category, keep individual detail inside the review with the named owner, and never put full card numbers into an artifact at all.

### equity-cap-table-desk
Requires: the cap table system of record, board consents and written approvals authorizing every grant, the equity incentive plan and its pool authorization, grant agreements with vesting schedules, the current independent valuation with its date, the option ledger including exercises, forfeitures, and cancellations, the payroll system for the tax treatment of exercises and vesting, the share classes with their rights, prior financing documents.
Owns: the cap table tied back to board consents grant by grant with any difference named, the option pool position showing authorized, granted, exercised, forfeited, and available, the stock compensation expense for the period with the model, the inputs, the expected term basis, and the forfeiture treatment behind it, the vesting and expense schedule roll-forward, the fully diluted share count with exactly what is included and what is not, dilution and preference analysis where a waterfall is requested, the valuation position including whether the current valuation has aged past its usable window, and the grants that exist in the ledger without an authorizing consent, reported as unauthorized rather than presumed approved.
Hands to: `month-end-close-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Equity is issued by the board and by nobody else. Recording, promising, or repricing a grant without the consent that authorizes it creates a security that does not legally exist, and the discovery usually happens during diligence when it is most expensive. Prepare the grant schedule and the expense; the board approves the equity.

### month-end-close-desk
Requires: the close calendar with tasks, owners, and dependencies, the subledger close status for revenue, receivables, payables, payroll, fixed assets, and equity, the cutoff date and evidence that transaction capture actually stopped, prepared journal entries with their support, prior period accruals and their reversals, the trial balance, the flux thresholds and the prior period comparatives, open items carried from last close.
Owns: the close calendar with each task's state and the dependency that is holding up anything late, the journal entry package where every entry carries its support, its preparer, and a reviewer who is not the preparer, cutoff testing across revenue, expense, and inventory at the period boundary, accrual completeness established from what was received, contracted, and consumed rather than from what happened to be invoiced, reversing entry management so last month's accrual does not double count this month's invoice, the flux review against the reconciled trial balance with an explanation for every threshold breach and the evidence behind it, intercompany positions with both sides agreed before elimination, the open items blocking close ranked by their effect on reported results, and the close binder that lets a reviewer follow any balance back to its support.
Hands to: `account-reconciliation-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Closing a period, reopening one, and posting into a period the controller has closed are all the controller's decisions. A closed period is audit visible and is unwound by finance rather than by an edit, which is why an entry that arrives late is posted to the next period with a note rather than backdated into the last one.

### account-reconciliation-desk
Requires: the trial balance for the period, subledger balances and their detail, bank statements for every account and entity, supporting schedules for prepaid, accrued, fixed asset, deferred revenue, and equity balances, prior period reconciliations with their open items, the reconciliation policy including which accounts require preparation at what frequency, the preparer and reviewer assignments.
Owns: the reconciliation set covering every account the policy requires, each showing the ledger balance, the supporting balance, and the difference, reconciling items with an amount, an age, and the evidence for each one, the unexplained residual stated at its full amount and never forced to zero, the subledger to control account tie for receivables, payables, revenue, fixed assets, and equity, the bank to book reconciliation with outstanding payments and deposits in transit listed individually, intercompany reconciliation with the out of balance owned by a named entity, aged reconciling items flagged where an item has survived several periods without resolution, the preparer and reviewer record showing separation between them, and the accounts that could not be reconciled, reported as unreconciled with what would resolve them.
Hands to: `tax-coordination-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. Statements would be produced over an account whose difference is unexplained or whose reconciling items are unsupported. The plug is the specific risk here: a difference forced to zero by an invented item is invisible for exactly as long as nobody samples it, and it is discovered by an auditor rather than by the person who created it. An honest unreconciled account with a stated amount is a finding the controller can act on; a reconciled-looking account with a fabricated item is a misstatement with a cover on it.

### tax-coordination-desk
Requires: the closed and reconciled pre-tax results by entity, the prior year returns and the return to provision true-up, the deferred tax roll-forward and the temporary difference schedule, jurisdictional activity establishing where the business has employees, property, and sales, indirect tax registrations and filing history, transfer pricing policy and intercompany agreements, the filings calendar with due dates, the external tax advisor's positions and correspondence.
Owns: the tax provision with current and deferred components computed from the closed results, the effective rate reconciliation bridging the statutory rate to the effective rate with every reconciling item named, the deferred tax roll-forward with temporary differences supported, the valuation allowance position with the positive and negative evidence weighed rather than asserted, nexus analysis identifying jurisdictions where activity has created an obligation and registration has not followed, with the exposure quantified and the exposure period stated, the indirect tax position covering registrations, rates applied on invoices, and any accrual for uncollected tax, the filings calendar with owners and preparation state, transfer pricing documentation status, and the positions that require the external advisor rather than an internal conclusion, routed rather than answered.
Hands to: `financial-reporting-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A tax return is signed and filed by an authorized person and creates a legal position with an authority that can examine it. A material position, a voluntary disclosure, a valuation allowance release, and any uncertain position belong to the tax advisor and the officer who signs. This desk prepares the workpaper and quantifies the exposure; it does not file, and it does not conclude on a position the advisor owns.

### financial-reporting-desk
Requires: the closed and reconciled trial balance with the tax provision posted, the consolidation structure with intercompany eliminations complete, prior period statements and comparatives with any restatement history, the disclosure requirements the framework imposes, the board or investor reporting template and its distribution list, the non-GAAP definitions and their reconciliations, covenant certificates and the definitions the credit agreement uses, the period status.
Owns: the financial statements covering income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, and equity roll-forward, with the cash flow statement built from the movement in the balance sheet rather than assembled independently, the consolidation with eliminations shown and any residual out of balance named, the disclosure set required by the framework with each note's preparation state, the board package with the narrative that explains what the statements mean and what changed, every non-GAAP or operating measure carrying its definition and its reconciliation to the nearest reported figure, prior period reclassifications with whether comparatives were restated stated explicitly, covenant computations using the definitions the agreement actually writes rather than the ones finance uses internally, and the figures that could not be supported, reported as unsupported rather than presented alongside the ones that were.
Hands to: `cash-flow-treasury-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. Statements would be distributed outside the company carrying an unreconciled account, an unposted material accrual, a non-GAAP measure without its reconciliation, or a period whose status is not what the cover says. Issued statements are relied upon, quoted, and filed, and a correction never reaches everyone who read the original. This is the most pressured halt in the suite, because the board date is always fixed and the ledger is always still moving.

### cash-flow-treasury-desk
Requires: bank statements and current balances by account and entity, the receivable aging with expected collection timing, the payable position with its payment dates, payroll and tax payment calendars, debt facilities with their amortization and covenant tests, committed spend and subscription renewals, the plan or forecast for the operating baseline, foreign currency positions and any restrictions on moving cash between entities.
Owns: the cash position by account and entity with the statement date behind each balance, the direct cash forecast over the requested horizon built from receipts and disbursements with a timing basis for each line rather than a smoothed run rate, the projected low point with the week it occurs, runway with the burn definition stated and the periods averaged named, working capital movements explaining the gap between profit and cash, covenant headroom computed using the agreement's own definitions with the test date, trapped cash where a balance exists in an entity that cannot fund the obligation that needs it, the funding actions available with their lead times, and the forecast accuracy of prior periods measured rather than claimed.
Hands to: `saas-metrics-reporting-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A runway or covenant figure would go to the board, a lender, or an investor without the bank statements and the facility terms behind it. Runway is the number that drives hiring freezes, bridge rounds, and layoffs, and a covenant computation that uses the internal definition rather than the agreement's definition can report headroom where a breach exists. Both are figures where being approximately right is not a category that exists.

### saas-metrics-reporting-desk
Requires: the contract base with amounts, terms, start dates, and any non-recurring components, recognized revenue by stream from the reporting stage, the customer and cohort structure, prior period metric values with the definitions that produced them, churn and downgrade events with their effective dates, sales and marketing spend by period for efficiency metrics, cash and burn figures from the treasury stage, the definitions document where the company has written its metrics down.
Owns: ARR and its bridge from opening through new, expansion, contraction, and churn to closing, with the bridge closing exactly and built once across the whole customer base, the annualization rule stated including how multi-year, usage, and services components are treated, the reconciliation between the run rate and recognized revenue that shows why they legitimately differ, net and gross revenue retention with the cohort, the window, and the treatment of upsell and downgrade, logo and revenue churn defined separately, burn multiple with both inputs named, customer acquisition payback and magic number with the specific costs included, growth and margin composition where a rule of forty style measure is requested, the definition change register because a metric that improved through redefinition is the most common way a trend misleads, and the metrics the contract data cannot yet support, named rather than approximated.
Hands to: `budget-planning-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A metric would go to investors or a board without the contract base behind it, or a run rate would be presented where a reader will read it as revenue. These metrics leave the company, get built into valuations and covenants, and are diligenced line by line later; an ARR figure that cannot be rebuilt from the contract base during diligence costs more than the round it was prepared for.

### budget-planning-desk
Requires: the closed actuals for the baseline period, the headcount plan with roles, start dates, and fully loaded cost assumptions, the revenue plan with its drivers and the pipeline or contract coverage behind it, departmental input and the budget holders who own each line, contractual commitments and renewals already in force, the planning calendar and its submission dates, the prior plan with its actual outcome, board expectations or guidance already communicated.
Owns: the operating plan by department and by account with a named holder on every line, the driver model showing which operational assumptions move which financial lines, headcount as the largest and most schedule-sensitive driver with start date timing modeled rather than annualized, committed costs separated from discretionary ones so a cut conversation has somewhere to start, the revenue build with its coverage basis, the assumption register naming what each line depends on and what would break it, the reconciliation between the bottom-up departmental build and any top-down target with the gap owned rather than allocated silently, prior plan accuracy measured to calibrate this one, and the lines no holder has accepted, reported as unowned rather than assigned by inference.
Hands to: `forecast-scenario-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A budget of record commits spending authority and becomes the number every department is measured against for the year. Setting or changing one belongs to the executive team and, where the company has one, the board. A plan quietly derived by finance is a target nobody agreed to defend, and the first variance conversation is about the plan rather than about the spending.

### forecast-scenario-desk
Requires: the approved plan, actuals to date with the period status of each, the drivers and their current values, known step changes such as launches, contract starts and ends, hires, and renewals, pipeline and contract coverage for the revenue view, cash constraints from the treasury stage, prior forecast accuracy, external guidance already given, the horizon the decision needs.
Owns: the reforecast with actuals to date and a projection for the remainder, stated so a reader can see where measurement ends and projection begins, the method with its drivers and their sources, scenarios where each is separated by a specific named assumption rather than by a percentage applied to the base, the step changes that break the trend called out individually because a run rate cannot see a contract that ends, the sensitivity showing which assumptions actually move the outcome, the cash and runway consequence of each scenario, the position against external guidance with the gap quantified, forecast accuracy measured against prior periods with the method stated, and the trigger points where a scenario becomes the base case so the decision is prepared before it is urgent.
Hands to: `variance-analysis-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A forecast would leave the company as guidance, go into a fundraising or lending process, or be used as a covenant projection without the actuals and the driver evidence behind it. A projection that a reader treats as a commitment is a different instrument from an internal planning view, and the difference is entirely in who received it.

### variance-analysis-desk
Requires: the closed actuals, the plan or the forecast being measured against with its version identified, the driver values for both, the department and cost center structure with its owners, the prior period reclassifications that make a comparison uneven, the materiality threshold for investigation, prior variance explanations and whether the actions taken worked.
Owns: the variance set at the level a holder can act on, with the plan version named because a variance against the original plan and against the current forecast are different statements, the decomposition separating price, volume, mix, timing, and classification effects, timing differences distinguished from run rate changes because they need opposite responses and the first one resolves itself, the classification variances where the money did not move but the account did, explanations grounded in what happened operationally rather than in what account the charge landed in, the owner per material variance and the action with a date, the variances that recur period after period, flagged as a planning problem rather than re-explained each month, and the movements that could not be explained from available evidence, reported as unexplained with what would explain them.
Hands to: `internal-controls-desk`, and back into `forecast-scenario-desk` where the variance changes the outlook.
Hard halt: source conflict. The actuals, the plan version, and the department structure disagree, typically because a reorganization moved cost centers or a reclassification moved accounts without restating the comparison. A variance computed across a structural change measures the change rather than the business, and the resulting conversation holds a manager accountable for a mapping decision.

### internal-controls-desk
Requires: the control framework in use and the risks it is meant to address, the process narratives or flow documentation for revenue, procure to pay, payroll, close, and treasury, system access and role assignments across the ERP, the banking platform, and the billing system, the delegation of authority matrix, evidence of control operation for the period, prior deficiencies and their remediation state, audit findings and management letters.
Owns: the control matrix mapping each control to the risk it addresses, its owner, its frequency, and the evidence that shows it operated, segregation of duties analysis across the systems that matter with the specific role combinations that create the conflict, particularly where one person can create a vendor and release a payment or post an entry and reconcile the account it hits, access review findings including access that outlived the role that needed it, the deficiency evaluation with severity reasoned from the magnitude that could go undetected rather than from how uncomfortable the finding is, compensating controls where a conflict cannot be resolved by headcount, the remediation plan with owners and dates, and the controls that exist on paper and produce no evidence of operation, reported as undocumented rather than assumed effective.
Hands to: `audit-support-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Concluding on the severity of a deficiency, and above all concluding that one is a material weakness, is a judgment with disclosure and audit consequences that belongs to the controller and the auditor. Equally, granting an exception to a control or accepting a segregation conflict is management accepting a risk, and it is accepted by a named person rather than absorbed into a document.

### audit-support-desk
Requires: the audit engagement scope and timeline, the prepared by client request list, the close binder and reconciliation set, contracts and supporting documents for sampled items, the trial balance and the general ledger detail, prior year workpapers and the adjustments they produced, the control documentation, management representation requirements, the responses already given to auditor questions.
Owns: the request list with an owner, a due date, and a state per item, support packages assembled so a sampled item can be traced from the ledger to the document without a follow-up request, the tie-out between the statements and the trial balance, walkthrough documentation describing what the process actually does rather than what the narrative says it does, the sample response record covering the population, the selection basis, and every exception found, the proposed adjustment log showing amount, accounts, whether it was booked or passed, and the reasoning, the summary of unadjusted differences evaluated against materiality in aggregate rather than item by item, the management representation items with the specific assertion each requires and who is being asked to sign it, and the requests that cannot be satisfied from available records, reported as unavailable with the reason.
Hands to: `finance-accounting-command-desk` for the engagement record, and back into whichever desk owns the account an adjustment or finding touches.
Hard halt: approval. Nothing goes to an auditor without the controller or the officer who owns the relationship. A representation is an assertion by management with personal consequences attached, an answer to an auditor question becomes audit evidence the moment it is given, and an explanation offered informally is hard to withdraw once it is in a workpaper.

## Packet rule

Every stage updates `finance_packet` as defined in `references/suite-workflow-contract.md` before handing off. Source facts, assumptions, approvals, open items, and unexplained differences accumulate across stages and are never dropped to keep an artifact short. An item removed from an open list is removed with its resolution and the period it was resolved in, because the same aged reconciling item, the same recurring variance, and the same segregation conflict resurface every period, and the useful record is what was decided about them last time and why.
